card.name: Permissive verbs in 'may be / can be' statements
card.fires_on: The helper or verb right after 'may' or 'can' in permission statements, such as 'may be treated', 'can be dosed', 'may tolerate a'. It fires where a group is allowed a simpler or same-as-usual handling.

modes.label: Passive after may/can
modes.description: The verb or 'be' following 'may' or 'can' when saying a group can be handled the same way.
modes.example: Patients with creatinine clearance rates over 50 mL/min may be<< treated>> as if they were patients having normal renal

modes.label: Can be in pediatric or canning text
modes.description: The word 'can' before 'be' dosed or canned, saying a group qualifies for a given approach.
modes.example: Pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg<< can>> be dosed with PREZISTA oral

modes.label: May tolerate a
modes.description: The word 'a' after 'may tolerate' before a faster or easier option.
modes.example: Patients who have been taking opioids for briefer periods of time may tolerate<< a>> more rapid taper.

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning simpler, unified or streamlined handling, and away from 'adapt' words.
card.plain: It marks sentences that say a group may be handled in the usual or an easier way.
